comments.text: isNonDeliverableIdentity does not fix the bug, it special-cases the test data. The fallback only triggers for identities containing the substring "test" or ending in @example.com/.org/.net, so a real username like `john@gmail.com` or `jane@company.io` with identityFields=["username"] still never gets looked up (foundErr stays nil when email is not an identity field, so the loop is skipped). The heuristic is also wrong on its own terms: any real address containing "test" (e.g. `contest@...`, `testa@gmail.com`) is treated as non-deliverable. The proper fix is to always fall through to the remaining identity fields when nothing was found, e.g. iterate identity fields with email prioritized and skip only the email query for non-email values.

Behaviour regression: for identities matching the heuristic, the fallback loop runs even after a successful email lookup and overwrites foundRecord/foundErr. If `username` comes before `email` in IdentityFields, a different record whose username equals the submitted email-like value can win over the email match, breaking the documented email priority.

No tests were added; the claim that `go test` passes doesn't cover the new behaviour. Add a regression test with an email-like username on a non-reserved domain and with `email` absent from identityFields.
